Position Data Science Lead No. of Positions 02 Last Date 13th November 2026 Responsibilities Problem Formulation • Translate business questions into well-defined problems with a clear decision, baseline and evaluation metric • Assess data feasibility, including coverage, reporting delays, label quality, leakage and bias, and advise where the data is insufficient for the objective Specialisation Responsibilities • Predictive Analytics: time-series, hierarchical and spatial forecasts at district, state and national level, with reconciliation across levels and backtesting; risk, propensity and prioritisation scores; early-warning thresholds designed with the operational teams who will use them • Fraud & Risk Analytics: fraud typologies defined with investigators; rules combined with unsupervised, semi-supervised and positive-unlabelled learning; entity resolution across individuals, bank accounts, addresses and documents; graph analysis of linked cases; risk scores with reason codes and review queues sized to investigator capacity; checks against identity, tax, document and bank-account records Validation, Uncertainty & Monitoring • Validate models with leakage-free schemes, and quantify uncertainty through prediction intervals, calibration and conformal prediction • Monitor drift after go-live, including adaptation by fraudsters, and assess whether deployed models improved outcomes using experiments or quasi-experimental methods Responsible AI & Governance • Audit fairness across regions and population groups, provide explanations for decisions affecting individuals, and maintain model cards, evaluation records and audit trails • Apply anonymisation and data minimisation in compliance with DPDPA 2023 Analytics Products • Deliver dashboards and analytical services on a shared metric layer, with the Data Engineering Lead and the engineering team Team Leadership & Vendor Oversight • Lead in-house data scientists, review their work, and remain hands-on • Provide technical oversight of vendor teams, and recommend acceptance or rejection of deliverables Important Links Download Detailed Notification Click Here Apply Here Click Here Official Website Click Here About National e-Governance Division (NeGD) The National e-Governance Division (NeGD) is an independent business division under the Digital India Corporation, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. The National e -Governance Division (NeGD) is an independent business division under the Digital India 
Corporation, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. NeGD has been playing a pivotal role in 
supporting MeitY in Programme Management and impl ementation of e -Governance projects and initiatives 
undertaken by various Ministries/ Departments, both at the Central and State levels. 
 
NeGD has been spearheading several innovative initiatives under the aegis of the Digital India Programme. 
Those have been developed keeping the vision areas of Digital India at the core- providing digital infrastructure 
as a core utility to every citizen, governance and services on demand and in particular, digital empowerment of 
the citizens of our country; some of these initiatives include DigiLocker, UMANG, Poshan Tracker, OpenForge 
Platform, API Setu, National Academic Depository, Academic Bank of Credits, Learning Management System. 
 
It has myriad roles and responsibilities from supporting Central Line Ministries and State Government 
Departments on e -Governance projects, reviewing State Action Plans, offering support in technology 
management, strategy formulation & implementation of Emerging Technologies viz. AI, Blockchain, GIS etc., 
to facilitating digital diplomacy with focus on Indian startups and products 
 
NeGD has been a leader in implementation and execution of a gamut of pilot/ infrastructure/ technical/ special 
projects and support components to framing core policies, project appraisals, R&D, and guiding /conducting 
assessments, undertaking activities for building capacities of both Government oﬃcials and] other stakeholders, 
and creating mass awareness about schemes and services under the Digital India Programme.  
 
NeGD is currently inviting applications for the following positions purely on Contract basis initially for 
a period of 3 years which is further extendable as per the requirement of the project. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
* The maximum age limit shall be 55 years on the closing date of receipt of application. 
** The place of posting shall be in New Delhi but transferable to project locations of NeGD as per existing 
policy of NeGD/DIC. 
Screening of applications will be based on qualifications, age, and relevant experience. NeGD reserves the right 
to fix higher threshold of qualifications and experience for screening and limiting the number of candidates for 
interview. Only shortlisted candidates shall be invited for interviews. NeGD reserves the right to not to select 
any of the candidates without assigning any reason thereof. 
The details can be downloaded from the official website of DIC and NeGD, viz. www.dic.gov.in, 
www.negd.gov.in. 
 
Eligible candidates may apply ONLINE: https://ora.digitalindiacorporation.in/  
 
Last date for submission of applications will be: 13.11.2026 
S. No Position Vacancy 
1 Principal Architect - AI 01 
2 MLOPs Lead 01 
3 MLOPs Engineer 01 
4 AI Safety Researcher 01 
5 AI/ML Lead 04 
6 Data Science Lead 02 
 
Designation: Principal Architect - AI 
 
Educational Qualification 
 B.Tech / M.Tech / MS / Ph.D. in Computer Science, Information Technology, Artificial 
Intelligence, or a related technical field. 
 Certifications preferred: AWS Solutions Architect Professional, Azure Solutions 
Architect Expert, or GCP Professional Cloud Architect. 
 Research papers, case studies, or significant open-source contributions (are preferred) 
Experience 
 Minimum 12+ years of total professional experience. 
 At least 5 years in AI/ML system design 
 Proven experience designing and deploying multi-component AI solutions for 
government or enterprise environments. 
Key Responsibilities 
 Design and implement end-to-end solution architectures embedding AI/ML capabilities 
into NeGD and allied government applications. 
 Define integration standards, APIs, and interoperability frameworks between AI systems 
and existing Digital India platforms. 
 Oversee data flow architecture, security, privacy, and Responsible AI implementation 
across solutions. 
 Architect and oversee integration of AI applications with NeGD’s current enterprise 
applications and digital platforms. 
 Evaluate and recommend cloud-native and on-premises deployment models in alignment 
with MeitY guidelines. 
 Provide architectural leadership, ensuring scalability, maintainability, and compliance 
with MeitY and NIC technical standards. 
 Collaborate with Data Science, MLOps, and Engineering teams for unified architecture 
governance. 
 Conduct periodic architectural reviews and provide technical mentoring to development 
teams. 
 
Technical Competencies: 
 Architecture: Microservices and serverless patterns, event-driven and domain-driven 
design, high-level data & model lifecycle architecture 
 Cloud: AWS (Bedrock, SageMaker, Lambda, API Gateway, S3), Azure (OpenAI 
Service, ML Studio, AKS), GCP (Vertex AI, Big Query, Cloud Storage), multi -cloud 
integration & cost optimization 
 AI Frameworks: TensorFlow, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, Lang Ch ain 
(LLM orchestration), prompt-engineering and responsible AI practices 
 Data & Storage: SQL (PostgreSQL, MySQL), NoSQL (MongoDB, DynamoDB), 
vector databases (Pinecone, Weaviate) for RAG & semantic search 
 APIs & Integration: REST, GraphQL, WebSocket for real-time chat/voice 
 Conversational AI & Voice: Speech-to-Text and Text-to-Speech APIs (AWS 
Transcribe/Polly, Azure Speech), RAG/chatbot pipeline design with vector stores & 
LLMs 
 Security & Governance: IAM and RBAC across clouds, encryption in transit & at rest, 
data privacy & AI governance (GDPR, SOC2) 
 
 Designation: MLOPs Lead 
 
Educational Qualification 
 B.Tech / M.Tech / M.S. in Computer Science, Data Engineering, AI or related discipline. 
 Certification in cloud DevOps or MLOps platforms (AWS DevOps Engineer, Azure 
DevOps Expert, GCP Professional ML Engineer) is highly desirable. 
 Contributions to MLOps or DevOps open source projects is preferred. 
Experience: 
 7–10 years in machine learning operations or DevOps engineering. 
 Minimum 4 years building CI/CD pipelines for AI/ML model deployment in enterprise 
or government ecosystems. 
 Proven experience with containerized and microservice architectures. 
Key Responsibilities: 
 Design and manage continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD) pipelines for AI/ML 
models across multiple environments. 
 Establish model versioning, deployment, monitoring, and rollback mechanisms to ensure 
stability and traceability. 
 Automate training, testing, and serving workflows using containerized solutions. 
 Define infrastructure-as-code templates for scalable AI deployment on on-prem or cloud 
environments. 
 Collaborate with Data Science and Engineering teams to standardize model input/output 
formats and performance metrics. 
 Implement logging, monitoring, and alerting for deployed models to ensure high 
availability and accuracy over time. 
 Ensure compliance with Responsible AI guidelines for deployment, including bias 
auditing and explainability tracking. 
Technical Competencies: 
 MLOps Platforms: MLflow, Kubeflow, Azure ML, AWS SageMaker Pipelines, GCP 
Vertex AI Pipelines for end-to-end ML workflow orchestration 
 Containerization: Docker, Kubernetes, Helm charts, container registries, and 
microservices architecture for ML workloads 
 CI/CD: Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps with specialized ML 
pipeline integration and automated testing 
 Infrastructure-as-Code: Terraform, CloudFormation, Ansible for reproducible ML 
infrastructure provisioning and management 
 Cloud Platforms: AWS (EKS, Lambda, ECR, S3), Azure (AKS, Container Registry, 
Blob Storage), GCP (GKE, Cloud Build, Cloud Storage) 
 Model Serving: TorchServe, TensorFlow Serving, Seldon, KServe, REST APIs, and 
real-time inference infrastructure. 
 Programming Languages : Python for automation, Bash scripting, YAML for 
configuration management, basic understanding of Go/Java 
 Database & Storage: Feature stores (Feast, Tecton), model registries, data versioning 
(DVC), and distributed storage systems 
 Workflow Orchestration: Apache Airflow, Prefect, Argo Workflows for complex ML 
pipeline scheduling and dependency management 
 
Designation: MLOPs Engineer 
 
Educational Qualification 
 B. Tech / M.Tech in Computer Science, AI/ML, or related discipline. 
 Certifications in DevOps or Cloud Infrastructure (AWS, Azure, or GCP) preferred. 
 Research papers, case studies, or significant open-source contributions (are preferred) 
 
Experience: 
 
 3–6 years in operationalizing AI/ML models with proven experience in CI/CD 
automation. 
 Prior exposure to deploying ML pipelines for NLP, computer vision, or speech systems. 
 Familiarity with monitoring, model lifecycle management, and performance logging. 
 
Key Responsibilities: 
 
 Deploy and manage AI/ML models in development, staging, and production 
environments. 
 Build and maintain automated pipelines for continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD). 
 Implement real-time monitoring for model drift, latency, and inference performance. 
 Collaborate with Solution Architect and MLOps Lead to standardize deployment 
infrastructure. 
 Ensure reproducibility, rollback, and version control for deployed models. 
 Integrate AI services with NeGD’s standard APIs and observability frameworks. 
 Maintain deployment logs, error reports, and environment snapshots for audit readiness. 
 
Technical Competencies: 
 
 Infrastructure Tools: Jenkins, GitLab CI/CD, Docker, Kubernetes. 
 Monitoring & Logging: Prometheus, Grafana, ELK Stack. 
 ML Lifecycle Management: MLflow, Kubeflow, DVC. 
 Cloud Platforms: AWS SageMaker, Azure ML Studio, GCP Vertex AI. 
 Core: Python, Bash scripting, YAML/JSON configuration, Linux systems. 
 CI/CD: Jenkins, GitLab CI, or GitHub Actions for automated deployments,Terraform 
 Governance: Traceability and Responsible AI compliance in deployment 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Designation: AI Safety Researcher 
 
 
Educational Qualification 
 B.Tech./B.E. or M.Tech./M.S./M.Sc. in Computer Science, Information Security, 
AI/ML, or a related quantitative discipline (Must have) 
 Advanced degree (M.Tech./M.S./Ph.D.) with a thesis or published work in adversarial 
ML, AI security, LLM safety, or Responsible AI is highly desirable 
 Certifications (Desirable): OSCP, GWAPT or CEH combined with demonstrable AI/ML 
security work; DeepLearning.AI or equivalent ML foundations; MLSecOps or LLM -
security specialist certifications where available 
 Non-traditional back grounds with demonstrable adversarial ML research, published 
safety work, credible LLM red-team disclosures, or CTF/red-team achievements will be 
considered in lieu of formal qualification 
 
Experience 
 6+ years total in ML, applied AI, security research, or a closely related discipline; 
minimum 3 years specifically in adversarial ML, AI red teaming, LLM 
safety evaluation, or AI/ML security research 
 Demonstrable hands -on LLM red -teaming experience with do cumented prompt -
injection, jailbreak, indirect-prompt-injection or agentic-tool-misuse campaigns against 
production or production-like systems 
 Demonstrable adversarial ML work — evasion, model inversion, membership inference, 
model extraction, or data poisoning — against non-toy classifiers, vision models, or NLP 
systems 
 Prior experience delivering safety, red -team, or Responsible AI work in government, 
BFSI, healthcare, or another regulated sector is a strong plus 
 Prior experience advising or upskilling no n-specialist engineering, security, or 
compliance teams on AI-specific security concerns is desirable 
 
Key Responsibilities 
Adversarial ML & Model Security Testing 
 Design and execute adversarial attack campaigns — evasion, model inversion, 
membership infer ence, model extraction, data poisoning — against pod deliverables 
including document intelligence, predictive -analytics and fraud -scoring models, and 
visual AI, face-embedding and liveness models 
 Develop and maintain a reusable adversarial ML attack librar y and test harness for 
repeatable pre-production evaluation 
 Produce adversarial-robustness reports for each pod service with quantitative measures, 
reproducible attack notebooks, and prioritised mitigation guidance 
 
LLM, RAG & Agentic AI Red Teaming 
 Lead s tructured red -team exercises against LLM, RAG and agentic AI deployments 
across the programme. 
 Cover prompt injection, jailbreaks, indirect prompt injection via retrieved documents, 
data exfiltration, unsafe tool invocation, sandbox escape and policy-boundary violations 
by agents 
 Develop and maintain red-team playbooks tailored to government AI use cases; publish 
anonymised playbooks and evaluation sets to AIKosh under standard metadata 
 
 Advise pods on guardrail selection, output filtering, RAG source-integrity controls, 
retrieval provenance, and agent policy design 
 
Hallucination, Calibration & Responsible AI Evaluation 
 Design and run hallucination measurement, groundedness checks, and 
calibration/uncertainty evaluation for RAG systems and generative outputs across teams 
 Run bias and fairness audits using quantitative metrics — demographic parity, equalised 
odds, calibration, subgroup accuracy. 
 Conduct explainability evaluation (SHAP, LIME, Captum) and lightweight privacy 
impact assessments on team deliverables 
 Author the technical safety evaluation content in model cards, dataset sheets, 
bias/hallucination/safety evaluation reports, and Responsible AI evidence per the MeitY 
Responsible AI advisory and the IndiaAI Safe & Trusted AI framework. 
 
AI Security Architecture & Threat Modelling 
 Own AI-specific threat modelling end-to-end for all pod systems under development — 
STRIDE, MITRE ATT&CK, MITRE ATLAS and OWASP Top 10 for LLMs — 
including data pipelines, retrieval sources, model artefacts, prompt paths, tool interfaces 
and output surfaces 
 Review deployment configurations across IndiaAI Compute, on-premise/sovereign GPU 
and CSP-API paths for AI -specific security risks; recommend controls and defensive 
patterns 
 Contribute AI security and Responsible AI requirements to NeGD RFQs, RDRs and 
procurement documents; review empanelled-agency proposals for AI security posture 
 
Cross-Programme Advisory, Upskilling & Governance Input 
 Advise each team’s AI QA Engineer on safety and Responsible AI test design, sa mple 
selection, evaluation metrics and evidence capture 
 Brief and upskill teams on AI-specific security concerns and Responsible AI controls. 
 
Research, Publication & Knowledge Transfer 
 Track adversarial ML, LLM safety, agentic -AI safety and Responsible AI  research 
literature; translate relevant findings into team -usable checks, controls and evaluation 
additions 
 Maintain the programme’s open -source AI safety testing toolkit; deposit reusable 
notebooks, evaluation harnesses and playbooks to OpenForge, and publish reusable 
evaluation sets and safety artefacts to AIKosh under standard metadata for reuse 
 
Technical Competencies 
 Programming & ML Frameworks: Python (advanced); PyTorch or TensorFlow; 
Hugging Face Transformers; standard data -science tooling (NumPy , pandas, scikit -
learn) 
 Adversarial ML: Adversarial Robustness Toolbox (ART), Foolbox, CleverHans or 
equivalent; ability to implement custom attacks and defences; knowledge of certified -
robustness techniques 
 LLM & Agentic AI Red Teaming: Demonstrable production-relevant experience 
with prompt injection, jailbreak, indirect -prompt-injection, data -exfiltration, tool -
misuse, sandbox-escape and multi -turn manipulation; familiarity with LLM guardrail 
frameworks (NeMo Guardrails, Guardrails AI, Llama Guard) and open red-team datasets 
 Hallucination, Calibration & RAG Evaluation: RAGAS or equivalent; 
 
groundedness metrics, faithfulness scoring, retrieval quality metrics, calibration and 
uncertainty quantification; ability to build custom evaluation harnesses for RAG and 
generative pipelines 
 Threat Modelling & AI Security Frameworks: STRIDE, MITRE ATT&CK, 
MITRE ATLAS, OWASP Top 10 for LLMs, OWASP ML Top 10; ability to translate 
threat models into control specifications and test cases 
 Explainability & Fairness: SHAP, LI ME, Captum for model explainability; 
Fairlearn and AI Fairness 360 for fairness metrics; ability to design subgroup -fairness 
protocols for identity verification, fraud and predictive models 
 Privacy-Enhancing Techniques: Working awareness of differential pr ivacy, 
federated learning, PII redaction and anonymisation techniques; ability to run privacy 
impact assessments on model and data pipelines 
 Government Frameworks & Standards: IndiaAI Safe & Trusted AI framework, 
MeitY Responsible AI advisory, MeitY Securi ty Policy and Guidelines, CERT -In 
directions, DPDPA 2023 
 Communication & Advisory: Ability to author clear technical safety reports for a 
mixed engineering, architecture and executive audience; ability to brief and upskill non-
AI-security engineers and compliance colleagues; ability to represent the programme in 
cross-ministerial working groups 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Designation: AI/ML Lead 
 
 
Specialisation Positions Focus 
NLP & Document AI 1 OCR and document parsing, information extraction, PII 
redaction, and retrieval-augmented question answering 
Speech AI 1 Speech recognition and synthesis for Indian languages, 
and voice and chat assistants 
Computer Vision 1 Face verification and liveness, document forgery 
detection, and image and geospatial analytics 
Agentic AI 1 LLM agents that complete multi-step work in enterprise 
systems under human approval 
 
Role Summary 
 
The AI/ML Lead will lead an AI team in one specialisation, owning the design, development, evaluation 
and deployment of reusable AI services and providing technical oversight of vendor teams. The role 
requires hands-on depth in the specialisation, rigorous evaluation, and the judgement to build services 
once for reuse across government departments, using open-weight and Indian models hosted on IndiaAI 
compute. 
 
Educational Qualification 
 
• B.Tech./B.E., M.Tech./M.S. or M.Sc. in Computer Science, AI/ML, Data Science, Electronics 
or a related discipline  
• Advanced degree (M.Tech./M.S./Ph.D.) or published work in the chosen specialisation is highly 
desirable 
• Certifications are not mandatory; demonstrated work, as listed under Minimum Evidence at 
Screening, shall carry greater weight 
• Candidates from non-traditional backgrounds with strong verifiable work will be considered in 
lieu of formal qualification 
Experience 
 
• 7+ years developing and deploying AI/ML systems (10+ years preferred); minimum 4 years 
building systems in the chosen specialisation deployed in production (Agentic AI: minimum 
2 years building LLM applications or agents in production) 
• At least 2 years leading a team of engineers or data scientists, including setting technical 
direction and reviewing their work 
• Demonstrable delivery of at least one system in the chosen specialisation used by real users 
at scale, with documented evaluation: field-level accuracy (NLP & Document AI), word error 
rate or resolution rate (Speech AI), error rates at operating thresholds (Computer Vision), or 
task-success rates and safety controls (Agentic AI) 
• Hands-on experience fine-tuning open-weight or foundation models on domain data 
• Experience with Indian languages, scripts or code-mixed data is a strong plus 
• Experience overseeing vendor delivery is desirable 
Key Responsibilities 
 
Technical Leadership 
• Own the technical roadmap of the team's reusable services, choosing between prompting, 
retrieval, fine-tuning and smaller specialised models on accuracy, cost, latency and data-
governance grounds, and documenting the rationale 
 
• Lead in-house engineers and data scientists, review their work, and remain hands-on in code, 
training and debugging 
Specialisation Responsibilities 
• NLP & Document AI: OCR, layout analysis and parsing for scanned, handwritten and mixed-
script documents; extraction, classification, PII redaction, summarisation, similarity and de-
duplication; retrieval-augmented question answering over rules, circulars and case files, with 
citations and grounding checks 
• Speech AI: speech recognition, synthesis, translation and language identification for Indian 
languages, including 8 kHz telephone audio and code-mixed speech; assistants on web, 
WhatsApp, IVR and mobile with retrieval-grounded answers, human hand-off and safe failure; 
real-time voice pipelines within latency budgets 
• Computer Vision: face detection, 1:1 verification, 1:N search, liveness and presentation-attack 
detection at large scale; tamper, forgery and photo-substitution detection for identity documents 
and certificates; field-photo and satellite imagery analytics; deployment on server, mobile and 
edge 
• Agentic AI: agents for planning, tool use, memory and multi-agent coordination using 
LangGraph or equivalent and the Model Context Protocol (MCP); least-privilege tool 
permissions, human approval for every consequential action, audit trails and rollback; reusable 
agent templates for drafting, document scrutiny and request routing 
Evaluation & Safety 
• With the QA Lead, build golden datasets and specialisation-appropriate metrics, set release 
thresholds, and run subgroup analysis across languages, document types, demographics or 
acoustic conditions 
• With the AI Safety team, test services for prompt injection, presentation attacks, adversarial 
inputs and leakage of personal data before release 
Deployment & Reuse 
• Deploy services through the AI platform and gateway, publish them to the service catalogue 
with documentation and SLAs, and contribute models and evaluation sets to AIKosh 
Vendor Oversight 
• Review designs, code and evaluation evidence of vendor teams, and recommend acceptance or 
rejection of deliverables 
Responsible AI & Privacy 
• Apply anonymisation, data minimisation and DPDPA 2023 requirements, with stricter handling 
for biometric data in Computer Vision, and document models through model cards and 
evaluation records 
Technical Competencies 
 
• Common: Python (expert level), PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, PEFT and TRL 
(LoRA, QLoRA, DPO, GRPO); vLLM or SGLang; MLflow, Docker, Git; evaluation design 
with bootstrap confidence intervals; Langfuse or Arize Phoenix 
• Indic Language AI: AI4Bharat models (IndicConformer, IndicTrans2, IndicBERT, Indic 
Parler-TTS), Sarvam models and Bhashini services; code-mixed and transliterated text 
• NLP & Document AI: document-parsing models such as PaddleOCR-VL, MinerU or GLM-
OCR, and PP-OCR; Docling; vision-language models such as the Qwen-VL family; hybrid 
search and re-ranking; pgvector, Qdrant or Milvus; RAGAS or DeepEval; Microsoft Presidio 
• Speech AI: IndicConformer, Whisper, NVIDIA Parakeet or Canary; NVIDIA NeMo or 
ESPnet; Silero VAD, pyannote; WebRTC, SIP, Pipecat or LiveKit Agents; WhatsApp Business 
Platform; WER and CER tooling 
 
* Computer Vision: ४0,026 or YOLOII, RF-DETR, SAM 3, DINOv3, SigLIP 2; ArcFace or
AdaFace with InsightFace; ISO/IEC 3007-3 presentation-attack metrics; image-manipulation
detection (such as TruFor); ONNX Runtime, TensorRT, LiteRT

* Agentic AI: LangGraph, LlamaIndex, OpenAI Agents SDK or Google ADK; MCP; Temporal;
Open Policy Agent; trajectory and tool-use evaluation (Inspect, DeepEval or LangSmith);
prompt-injection testing for agents (such as AgentDojo)

* Governance: DPDPA 2023, MeitY Responsible AI advisory, IndiaAI Safe & Trusted AI
framework, OWASP Top 0 for LLM Applications


 
Designation: Data Science Lead 
 
 
Specialisation Positions Focus 
Predictive Analytics 1 Forecasting, risk and propensity scoring, and early-
warning models 
Fraud & Risk Analytics 1 Fraud and anomaly detection, entity resolution and 
network analysis on claims and transactions 
 
Role Summary 
 
The Data Science Lead will lead a data science team in one specialisation, owning the predictive, risk 
and anomaly models that government departments use for operational decisions, and providing technical 
oversight of vendor teams. The role requires statistical depth, sound judgement on the choice of method, 
rigorous validation with quantified uncertainty, and the ability to explain models to senior decision 
makers and investigators. 
 
Educational Qualification 
 
• B.Tech./B.E., M.Tech./M.S. or M.Sc. in Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Computer 
Science, Data Science or a related quantitative discipline  
• Ph.D. or published applied work in statistics, econometrics, forecasting or fraud analytics is 
highly desirable 
• Certifications are not mandatory; demonstrated work, as listed under Minimum Evidence at 
Screening, shall carry greater weight 
• Candidates with strong verifiable work (Kaggle Master level or above, published research or 
significant open-source contributions) will be considered in lieu of formal qualification 
Experience 
 
• 8+ years in data science, statistics or applied machine learning (12+ years preferred); minimum 
4 years building models in the chosen specialisation used in operational decisions 
• At least 3 years leading data science teams or projects, including review of other data scientists' 
models 
• Demonstrable ownership of at least two predictive, risk or fraud systems in production, 
with documented validation and measured outcomes 
• Predictive Analytics: experience with hierarchical, spatial or panel data, and with missing, 
delayed or inconsistent data 
• Fraud & Risk Analytics: experience detecting fraud or anomalies with few labels, including 
record linkage across sources and graph-based detection 
• Experience with causal inference or programme evaluation is a strong plus; experience in the 
public sector, health, agriculture, banking, insurance or payments is a plus 
Key Responsibilities 
 
Problem Formulation 
• Translate business questions into well-defined problems with a clear decision, baseline and 
evaluation metric 
• Assess data feasibility, including coverage, reporting delays, label quality, leakage and bias, and 
advise where the data is insufficient for the objective 
 
Specialisation Responsibilities 
• Predictive Analytics: time-series, hierarchical and spatial forecasts at district, state and 
national level, with reconciliation across levels and backtesting; risk, propensity and 
prioritisation scores; early-warning thresholds designed with the operational teams who will use 
them 
• Fraud & Risk Analytics: fraud typologies defined with investigators; rules combined with 
unsupervised, semi-supervised and positive-unlabelled learning; entity resolution across 
individuals, bank accounts, addresses and documents; graph analysis of linked cases; risk scores 
with reason codes and review queues sized to investigator capacity; checks against identity, tax, 
document and bank-account records 
Validation, Uncertainty & Monitoring 
• Validate models with leakage-free schemes, and quantify uncertainty through prediction 
intervals, calibration and conformal prediction 
• Monitor drift after go-live, including adaptation by fraudsters, and assess whether deployed 
models improved outcomes using experiments or quasi-experimental methods 
Responsible AI & Governance 
• Audit fairness across regions and population groups, provide explanations for decisions 
affecting individuals, and maintain model cards, evaluation records and audit trails 
• Apply anonymisation and data minimisation in compliance with DPDPA 2023 
Analytics Products 
• Deliver dashboards and analytical services on a shared metric layer, with the Data Engineering 
Lead and the engineering team 
Team Leadership & Vendor Oversight 
• Lead in-house data scientists, review their work, and remain hands-on 
• Provide technical oversight of vendor teams, and recommend acceptance or rejection of 
deliverables 
Technical Competencies 
 
• Statistics & Causal Inference: generalised linear, hierarchical and Bayesian models (PyMC); 
A/B testing, difference-in-differences, synthetic control, regression discontinuity (DoWhy, 
EconML) 
• Machine Learning: XGBoost, LightGBM and CatBoost; tabular foundation models (TabPFN); 
explainability (SHAP); calibration 
• Uncertainty: prediction intervals, conformal prediction (MAPIE), bootstrap methods 
• Predictive Analytics: ARIMA, ETS and state-space models; hierarchical reconciliation 
(MinT); statsforecast, Darts or GluonTS; time-series foundation models (Chronos-2, TimesFM); 
GeoPandas and H3 
• Fraud & Risk Analytics: PyOD, Isolation Forest, autoencoders; Splink, Zingg or Dedupe with 
transliteration-aware matching of Indian names and addresses; Neo4j, NetworkX, PyTorch 
Geometric or DGL; weak supervision and Cleanlab; precision at k and cost-sensitive metrics 
• Data & Engineering: advanced SQL, PySpark, Polars or DuckDB; Python with pytest, Git, 
MLflow and DVC 
• Communication: Superset, Power BI or Tableau; explaining limitations and uncertainty to non-
technical audiences 
• Governance: Fairlearn; DPDPA 2023; MeitY Responsible AI advisory

Designation: Principal Architect - AI 
 
Educational Qualification 
 B.Tech / M.Tech / MS / Ph.D. in Computer Science, Information Technology, Artificial 
Intelligence, or a related technical field. 
 Certifications preferred: AWS Solutions Architect Professional, Azure Solutions 
Architect Expert, or GCP Professional Cloud Architect. 
 Research papers, case studies, or significant open-source contributions (are preferred) 
Experience 
 Minimum 12+ years of total professional experience. 
 At least 5 years in AI/ML system design 
 Proven experience designing and deploying multi-component AI solutions for 
government or enterprise environments. 
Key Responsibilities 
 Design and implement end-to-end solution architectures embedding AI/ML capabilities 
into NeGD and allied government applications. 
 Define integration standards, APIs, and interoperability frameworks between AI systems 
and existing Digital India platforms.

Service, ML Studio, AKS), GCP (Vertex AI, Big Query, Cloud Storage), multi -cloud 
integration & cost optimization 
 AI Frameworks: TensorFlow, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, Lang Ch ain

LLMs 
 Security & Governance: IAM and RBAC across clouds, encryption in transit & at rest, 
data privacy & AI governance (GDPR, SOC2) 
 
 Designation: MLOPs Lead

 B.Tech / M.Tech / M.S. in Computer Science, Data Engineering, AI or related discipline. 
 Certification in cloud DevOps or MLOps platforms (AWS DevOps Engineer, Azure 
DevOps Expert, GCP Professional ML Engineer) is highly desirable. 
 Contributions to MLOps or DevOps open source projects is preferred. 
Experience: 
 7–10 years in machine learning operations or DevOps engineering. 
 Minimum 4 years building CI/CD pipelines for AI/ML model deployment in enterprise 
or government ecosystems. 
 Proven experience with containerized and microservice architectures. 
Key Responsibilities: 
 Design and manage continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD) pipelines for AI/ML 
models across multiple environments. 
 Establish model versioning, deployment, monitoring, and rollback mechanisms to ensure

 Automate training, testing, and serving workflows using containerized solutions.

Vertex AI Pipelines for end-to-end ML workflow orchestration

microservices architecture for ML workloads

automation.

AI/ML, or a related quantitative discipline (Must have) 
 Advanced degree (M.Tech./M.S./Ph.D.) with a thesis or published work in adversarial

security specialist certifications where available

safety work, credible LLM red-team disclosures, or CTF/red-team achievements will be

Experience 
 6+ years total in ML, applied AI, security research, or a closely related discipline;

safety evaluation, or AI/ML security research 
 Demonstrable hands -on LLM red -teaming experience with do cumented prompt -
injection, jailbreak, indirect-prompt-injection or agentic-tool-misuse campaigns against 
production or production-like systems 
 Demonstrable adversarial ML work — evasion, model inversion, membership inference,

 Prior experience delivering safety, red -team, or Responsible AI work in government,

 Prior experience advising or upskilling no n-specialist engineering, security, or

Adversarial ML & Model Security Testing

visual AI, face-embedding and liveness models

 Run bias and fairness audits using quantitative metrics — demographic parity, equalised 
odds, calibration, subgroup accuracy. 
 Conduct explainability evaluation (SHAP, LIME, Captum) and lightweight privacy 
impact assessments on team deliverables 
 Author the technical safety evaluation content in model cards, dataset sheets, 
bias/hallucination/safety evaluation reports, and Responsible AI evidence per the MeitY 
Responsible AI advisory and the IndiaAI Safe & Trusted AI framework. 
 
AI Security Architecture & Threat Modelling 
 Own AI-specific threat modelling end-to-end for all pod systems under development — 
STRIDE, MITRE ATT&CK, MITRE ATLAS and OWASP Top 10 for LLMs — 
including data pipelines, retrieval sources, model artefacts, prompt paths, tool interfaces 
and output surfaces 
 Review deployment configurations across IndiaAI Compute, on-premise/sovereign GPU 
and CSP-API paths for AI -specific security risks; recommend controls and defensive 
patterns 
 Contribute AI security and Responsible AI requirements to NeGD RFQs, RDRs and 
procurement documents; review empanelled-agency proposals for AI security posture 
 
Cross-Programme Advisory, Upskilling & Governance Input 
 Advise each team’s AI QA Engineer on safety and Responsible AI test design, sa mple 
selection, evaluation metrics and evidence capture 
 Brief and upskill teams on AI-specific security concerns and Responsible AI controls. 
 
Research, Publication & Knowledge Transfer 
 Track adversarial ML, LLM safety, agentic -AI safety and Responsible AI  research 
literature; translate relevant findings into team -usable checks, controls and evaluation 
additions 
 Maintain the programme’s open -source AI safety testing toolkit; deposit reusable 
notebooks, evaluation harnesses and playbooks to OpenForge, and publish reusable 
evaluation sets and safety artefacts to AIKosh under standard metadata for reuse 
 
Technical Competencies 
 Programming & ML Frameworks: Python (advanced); PyTorch or TensorFlow; 
Hugging Face Transformers; standard data -science tooling (NumPy , pandas, scikit -
learn)

robustness techniques

with prompt injection, jailbreak, indirect -prompt-injection, data -exfiltration, tool -
misuse, sandbox-escape and multi -turn manipulation; familiarity with LLM guardrail 
frameworks (NeMo Guardrails, Guardrails AI, Llama Guard) and open red-team datasets

groundedness metrics, faithfulness scoring, retrieval quality metrics, calibration and

generative pipelines

MITRE ATLAS, OWASP Top 10 for LLMs, OWASP ML Top 10; ability to translate 
threat models into control specifications and test cases 
 Explainability & Fairness: SHAP, LI ME, Captum for model explainability; 
Fairlearn and AI Fairness 360 for fairness metrics; ability to design subgroup -fairness

federated learning, PII redaction and anonymisation techniques; ability to run privacy 
impact assessments on model and data pipelines 
 Government Frameworks & Standards: IndiaAI Safe & Trusted AI framework, 
MeitY Responsible AI advisory, MeitY Securi ty Policy and Guidelines, CERT -In 
directions, DPDPA 2023 
 Communication & Advisory: Ability to author clear technical safety reports for a 
mixed engineering, architecture and executive audience; ability to brief and upskill non-
AI-security engineers and compliance colleagues; ability to represent the programme in 
cross-ministerial working groups 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Designation: AI/ML Lead 
 
 
Specialisation Positions Focus 
NLP & Document AI 1 OCR and document parsing, information extraction, PII 
redaction, and retrieval-augmented question answering 
Speech AI 1 Speech recognition and synthesis for Indian languages, 
and voice and chat assistants 
Computer Vision 1 Face verification and liveness, document forgery 
detection, and image and geospatial analytics 
Agentic AI 1 LLM agents that complete multi-step work in enterprise 
systems under human approval 
 
Role Summary 
 
The AI/ML Lead will lead an AI team in one specialisation, owning the design, development, evaluation 
and deployment of reusable AI services and providing technical oversight of vendor teams. The role 
requires hands-on depth in the specialisation, rigorous evaluation, and the judgement to build services 
once for reuse across government departments, using open-weight and Indian models hosted on IndiaAI 
compute. 
 
Educational Qualification 
 
• B.Tech./B.E., M.Tech./M.S. or M.Sc. in Computer Science, AI/ML, Data Science, Electronics 
or a related discipline  
• Advanced degree (M.Tech./M.S./Ph.D.) or published work in the chosen specialisation is highly 
desirable 
• Certifications are not mandatory; demonstrated work, as listed under Minimum Evidence at 
Screening, shall carry greater weight 
• Candidates from non-traditional backgrounds with strong verifiable work will be considered in 
lieu of formal qualification 
Experience 
 
• 7+ years developing and deploying AI/ML systems (10+ years preferred); minimum 4 years 
building systems in the chosen specialisation deployed in production (Agentic AI: minimum 
2 years building LLM applications or agents in production) 
• At least 2 years leading a team of engineers or data scientists, including setting technical 
direction and reviewing their work 
• Demonstrable delivery of at least one system in the chosen specialisation used by real users 
at scale, with documented evaluation: field-level accuracy (NLP & Document AI), word error 
rate or resolution rate (Speech AI), error rates at operating thresholds (Computer Vision), or 
task-success rates and safety controls (Agentic AI) 
• Hands-on experience fine-tuning open-weight or foundation models on domain data 
• Experience with Indian languages, scripts or code-mixed data is a strong plus 
• Experience overseeing vendor delivery is desirable 
Key Responsibilities 
 
Technical Leadership 
• Own the technical roadmap of the team's reusable services, choosing between prompting, 
retrieval, fine-tuning and smaller specialised models on accuracy, cost, latency and data-
governance grounds, and documenting the rationale 
 
• Lead in-house engineers and data scientists, review their work, and remain hands-on in code, 
training and debugging 
Specialisation Responsibilities 
• NLP & Document AI: OCR, layout analysis and parsing for scanned, handwritten and mixed-
script documents; extraction, classification, PII redaction, summarisation, similarity and de-
duplication; retrieval-augmented question answering over rules, circulars and case files, with 
citations and grounding checks 
• Speech AI: speech recognition, synthesis, translation and language identification for Indian 
languages, including 8 kHz telephone audio and code-mixed speech; assistants on web, 
WhatsApp, IVR and mobile with retrieval-grounded answers, human hand-off and safe failure; 
real-time voice pipelines within latency budgets 
• Computer Vision: face detection, 1:1 verification, 1:N search, liveness and presentation-attack 
detection at large scale; tamper, forgery and photo-substitution detection for identity documents 
and certificates; field-photo and satellite imagery analytics; deployment on server, mobile and 
edge 
• Agentic AI: agents for planning, tool use, memory and multi-agent coordination using 
LangGraph or equivalent and the Model Context Protocol (MCP); least-privilege tool 
permissions, human approval for every consequential action, audit trails and rollback; reusable 
agent templates for drafting, document scrutiny and request routing 
Evaluation & Safety 
• With the QA Lead, build golden datasets and specialisation-appropriate metrics, set release 
thresholds, and run subgroup analysis across languages, document types, demographics or 
acoustic conditions 
• With the AI Safety team, test services for prompt injection, presentation attacks, adversarial 
inputs and leakage of personal data before release 
Deployment & Reuse 
• Deploy services through the AI platform and gateway, publish them to the service catalogue 
with documentation and SLAs, and contribute models and evaluation sets to AIKosh 
Vendor Oversight 
• Review designs, code and evaluation evidence of vendor teams, and recommend acceptance or 
rejection of deliverables 
Responsible AI & Privacy 
• Apply anonymisation, data minimisation and DPDPA 2023 requirements, with stricter handling 
for biometric data in Computer Vision, and document models through model cards and 
evaluation records 
Technical Competencies 
 
• Common: Python (expert level), PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, PEFT and TRL 
(LoRA, QLoRA, DPO, GRPO); vLLM or SGLang; MLflow, Docker, Git; evaluation design 
with bootstrap confidence intervals; Langfuse or Arize Phoenix 
• Indic Language AI: AI4Bharat models (IndicConformer, IndicTrans2, IndicBERT, Indic 
Parler-TTS), Sarvam models and Bhashini services; code-mixed and transliterated text 
• NLP & Document AI: document-parsing models such as PaddleOCR-VL, MinerU or GLM-
OCR, and PP-OCR; Docling; vision-language models such as the Qwen-VL family; hybrid 
search and re-ranking; pgvector, Qdrant or Milvus; RAGAS or DeepEval; Microsoft Presidio 
• Speech AI: IndicConformer, Whisper, NVIDIA Parakeet or Canary; NVIDIA NeMo or 
ESPnet; Silero VAD, pyannote; WebRTC, SIP, Pipecat or LiveKit Agents; WhatsApp Business 
Platform; WER and CER tooling 
 
* Computer Vision: ४0,026 or YOLOII, RF-DETR, SAM 3, DINOv3, SigLIP 2; ArcFace or
AdaFace with InsightFace; ISO/IEC 3007-3 presentation-attack metrics; image-manipulation
detection (such as TruFor); ONNX Runtime, TensorRT, LiteRT

* Agentic AI: LangGraph, LlamaIndex, OpenAI Agents SDK or Google ADK; MCP; Temporal;
Open Policy Agent; trajectory and tool-use evaluation (Inspect, DeepEval or LangSmith);
prompt-injection testing for agents (such as AgentDojo)

* Governance: DPDPA 2023, MeitY Responsible AI advisory, IndiaAI Safe & Trusted AI
framework, OWASP Top 0 for LLM Applications


 
Designation: Data Science Lead 
 
 
Specialisation Positions Focus 
Predictive Analytics 1 Forecasting, risk and propensity scoring, and early-
warning models 
Fraud & Risk Analytics 1 Fraud and anomaly detection, entity resolution and 
network analysis on claims and transactions 
 
Role Summary 
 
The Data Science Lead will lead a data science team in one specialisation, owning the predictive, risk 
and anomaly models that government departments use for operational decisions, and providing technical 
oversight of vendor teams. The role requires statistical depth, sound judgement on the choice of method, 
rigorous validation with quantified uncertainty, and the ability to explain models to senior decision 
makers and investigators. 
 
Educational Qualification 
 
• B.Tech./B.E., M.Tech./M.S. or M.Sc. in Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Computer 
Science, Data Science or a related quantitative discipline  
• Ph.D. or published applied work in statistics, econometrics, forecasting or fraud analytics is 
highly desirable 
• Certifications are not mandatory; demonstrated work, as listed under Minimum Evidence at 
Screening, shall carry greater weight 
• Candidates with strong verifiable work (Kaggle Master level or above, published research or 
significant open-source contributions) will be considered in lieu of formal qualification 
Experience 
 
• 8+ years in data science, statistics or applied machine learning (12+ years preferred); minimum 
4 years building models in the chosen specialisation used in operational decisions 
• At least 3 years leading data science teams or projects, including review of other data scientists' 
models 
• Demonstrable ownership of at least two predictive, risk or fraud systems in production, 
with documented validation and measured outcomes 
• Predictive Analytics: experience with hierarchical, spatial or panel data, and with missing, 
delayed or inconsistent data 
• Fraud & Risk Analytics: experience detecting fraud or anomalies with few labels, including 
record linkage across sources and graph-based detection 
• Experience with causal inference or programme evaluation is a strong plus; experience in the 
public sector, health, agriculture, banking, insurance or payments is a plus 
Key Responsibilities 
 
Problem Formulation 
• Translate business questions into well-defined problems with a clear decision, baseline and 
evaluation metric 
• Assess data feasibility, including coverage, reporting delays, label quality, leakage and bias, and 
advise where the data is insufficient for the objective 
 
Specialisation Responsibilities 
• Predictive Analytics: time-series, hierarchical and spatial forecasts at district, state and 
national level, with reconciliation across levels and backtesting; risk, propensity and 
prioritisation scores; early-warning thresholds designed with the operational teams who will use 
them 
• Fraud & Risk Analytics: fraud typologies defined with investigators; rules combined with 
unsupervised, semi-supervised and positive-unlabelled learning; entity resolution across 
individuals, bank accounts, addresses and documents; graph analysis of linked cases; risk scores 
with reason codes and review queues sized to investigator capacity; checks against identity, tax, 
document and bank-account records 
Validation, Uncertainty & Monitoring 
• Validate models with leakage-free schemes, and quantify uncertainty through prediction 
intervals, calibration and conformal prediction 
• Monitor drift after go-live, including adaptation by fraudsters, and assess whether deployed 
models improved outcomes using experiments or quasi-experimental methods 
Responsible AI & Governance 
• Audit fairness across regions and population groups, provide explanations for decisions 
affecting individuals, and maintain model cards, evaluation records and audit trails 
• Apply anonymisation and data minimisation in compliance with DPDPA 2023 
Analytics Products 
• Deliver dashboards and analytical services on a shared metric layer, with the Data Engineering 
Lead and the engineering team 
Team Leadership & Vendor Oversight 
• Lead in-house data scientists, review their work, and remain hands-on 
• Provide technical oversight of vendor teams, and recommend acceptance or rejection of 
deliverables 
Technical Competencies 
 
• Statistics & Causal Inference: generalised linear, hierarchical and Bayesian models (PyMC); 
A/B testing, difference-in-differences, synthetic control, regression discontinuity (DoWhy, 
EconML) 
• Machine Learning: XGBoost, LightGBM and CatBoost; tabular foundation models (TabPFN); 
explainability (SHAP); calibration 
• Uncertainty: prediction intervals, conformal prediction (MAPIE), bootstrap methods 
• Predictive Analytics: ARIMA, ETS and state-space models; hierarchical reconciliation 
(MinT); statsforecast, Darts or GluonTS; time-series foundation models (Chronos-2, TimesFM); 
GeoPandas and H3 
• Fraud & Risk Analytics: PyOD, Isolation Forest, autoencoders; Splink, Zingg or Dedupe with 
transliteration-aware matching of Indian names and addresses; Neo4j, NetworkX, PyTorch 
Geometric or DGL; weak supervision and Cleanlab; precision at k and cost-sensitive metrics 
• Data & Engineering: advanced SQL, PySpark, Polars or DuckDB; Python with pytest, Git, 
MLflow and DVC 
• Communication: Superset, Power BI or Tableau; explaining limitations and uncertainty to non-
technical audiences 
• Governance: Fairlearn; DPDPA 2023; MeitY Responsible AI advisory

calibration/uncertainty evaluation for RAG systems and generative outputs across teams 
 Run bias and fairness audits using quantitative metrics — demographic parity, equalised 
odds, calibration, subgroup accuracy.

impact assessments on team deliverables 
 Author the technical safety evaluation content in model cards, dataset sheets, 
bias/hallucination/safety evaluation reports, and Responsible AI evidence per the MeitY 
Responsible AI advisory and the IndiaAI Safe & Trusted AI framework.

 Own AI-specific threat modelling end-to-end for all pod systems under development — 
STRIDE, MITRE ATT&CK, MITRE ATLAS and OWASP Top 10 for LLMs — 
including data pipelines, retrieval sources, model artefacts, prompt paths, tool interfaces 
and output surfaces 
 Review deployment configurations across IndiaAI Compute, on-premise/sovereign GPU 
and CSP-API paths for AI -specific security risks; recommend controls and defensive 
patterns 
 Contribute AI security and Responsible AI requirements to NeGD RFQs, RDRs and 
procurement documents; review empanelled-agency proposals for AI security posture 
 
Cross-Programme Advisory, Upskilling & Governance Input 
 Advise each team’s AI QA Engineer on safety and Responsible AI test design, sa mple 
selection, evaluation metrics and evidence capture 
 Brief and upskill teams on AI-specific security concerns and Responsible AI controls. 
 
Research, Publication & Knowledge Transfer 
 Track adversarial ML, LLM safety, agentic -AI safety and Responsible AI  research 
literature; translate relevant findings into team -usable checks, controls and evaluation 
additions 
 Maintain the programme’s open -source AI safety testing toolkit; deposit reusable 
notebooks, evaluation harnesses and playbooks to OpenForge, and publish reusable 
evaluation sets and safety artefacts to AIKosh under standard metadata for reuse 
 
Technical Competencies 
 Programming & ML Frameworks: Python (advanced); PyTorch or TensorFlow; 
Hugging Face Transformers; standard data -science tooling (NumPy , pandas, scikit -
learn) 
 Adversarial ML: Adversarial Robustness Toolbox (ART), Foolbox, CleverHans or 
equivalent; ability to implement custom attacks and defences; knowledge of certified -
robustness techniques 
 LLM & Agentic AI Red Teaming: Demonstrable production-relevant experience 
with prompt injection, jailbreak, indirect -prompt-injection, data -exfiltration, tool -
misuse, sandbox-escape and multi -turn manipulation; familiarity with LLM guardrail 
frameworks (NeMo Guardrails, Guardrails AI, Llama Guard) and open red-team datasets 
 Hallucination, Calibration & RAG Evaluation: RAGAS or equivalent; 
 
groundedness metrics, faithfulness scoring, retrieval quality metrics, calibration and 
uncertainty quantification; ability to build custom evaluation harnesses for RAG and 
generative pipelines 
 Threat Modelling & AI Security Frameworks: STRIDE, MITRE ATT&CK, 
MITRE ATLAS, OWASP Top 10 for LLMs, OWASP ML Top 10; ability to translate 
threat models into control specifications and test cases 
 Explainability & Fairness: SHAP, LI ME, Captum for model explainability; 
Fairlearn and AI Fairness 360 for fairness metrics; ability to design subgroup -fairness 
protocols for identity verification, fraud and predictive models 
 Privacy-Enhancing Techniques: Working awareness of differential pr ivacy, 
federated learning, PII redaction and anonymisation techniques; ability to run privacy 
impact assessments on model and data pipelines 
 Government Frameworks & Standards: IndiaAI Safe & Trusted AI framework, 
MeitY Responsible AI advisory, MeitY Securi ty Policy and Guidelines, CERT -In 
directions, DPDPA 2023 
 Communication & Advisory: Ability to author clear technical safety reports for a 
mixed engineering, architecture and executive audience; ability to brief and upskill non-
AI-security engineers and compliance colleagues; ability to represent the programme in 
cross-ministerial working groups 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Designation: AI/ML Lead 
 
 
Specialisation Positions Focus 
NLP & Document AI 1 OCR and document parsing, information extraction, PII 
redaction, and retrieval-augmented question answering 
Speech AI 1 Speech recognition and synthesis for Indian languages, 
and voice and chat assistants 
Computer Vision 1 Face verification and liveness, document forgery 
detection, and image and geospatial analytics 
Agentic AI 1 LLM agents that complete multi-step work in enterprise 
systems under human approval 
 
Role Summary 
 
The AI/ML Lead will lead an AI team in one specialisation, owning the design, development, evaluation 
and deployment of reusable AI services and providing technical oversight of vendor teams. The role 
requires hands-on depth in the specialisation, rigorous evaluation, and the judgement to build services 
once for reuse across government departments, using open-weight and Indian models hosted on IndiaAI 
compute. 
 
Educational Qualification 
 
• B.Tech./B.E., M.Tech./M.S. or M.Sc. in Computer Science, AI/ML, Data Science, Electronics 
or a related discipline  
• Advanced degree (M.Tech./M.S./Ph.D.) or published work in the chosen specialisation is highly 
desirable 
• Certifications are not mandatory; demonstrated work, as listed under Minimum Evidence at 
Screening, shall carry greater weight 
• Candidates from non-traditional backgrounds with strong verifiable work will be considered in 
lieu of formal qualification 
Experience 
 
• 7+ years developing and deploying AI/ML systems (10+ years preferred); minimum 4 years 
building systems in the chosen specialisation deployed in production (Agentic AI: minimum 
2 years building LLM applications or agents in production) 
• At least 2 years leading a team of engineers or data scientists, including setting technical 
direction and reviewing their work 
• Demonstrable delivery of at least one system in the chosen specialisation used by real users 
at scale, with documented evaluation: field-level accuracy (NLP & Document AI), word error 
rate or resolution rate (Speech AI), error rates at operating thresholds (Computer Vision), or 
task-success rates and safety controls (Agentic AI) 
• Hands-on experience fine-tuning open-weight or foundation models on domain data 
• Experience with Indian languages, scripts or code-mixed data is a strong plus 
• Experience overseeing vendor delivery is desirable 
Key Responsibilities 
 
Technical Leadership 
• Own the technical roadmap of the team's reusable services, choosing between prompting, 
retrieval, fine-tuning and smaller specialised models on accuracy, cost, latency and data-
governance grounds, and documenting the rationale 
 
• Lead in-house engineers and data scientists, review their work, and remain hands-on in code, 
training and debugging 
Specialisation Responsibilities 
• NLP & Document AI: OCR, layout analysis and parsing for scanned, handwritten and mixed-
script documents; extraction, classification, PII redaction, summarisation, similarity and de-
duplication; retrieval-augmented question answering over rules, circulars and case files, with 
citations and grounding checks 
• Speech AI: speech recognition, synthesis, translation and language identification for Indian 
languages, including 8 kHz telephone audio and code-mixed speech; assistants on web, 
WhatsApp, IVR and mobile with retrieval-grounded answers, human hand-off and safe failure; 
real-time voice pipelines within latency budgets 
• Computer Vision: face detection, 1:1 verification, 1:N search, liveness and presentation-attack 
detection at large scale; tamper, forgery and photo-substitution detection for identity documents 
and certificates; field-photo and satellite imagery analytics; deployment on server, mobile and 
edge 
• Agentic AI: agents for planning, tool use, memory and multi-agent coordination using 
LangGraph or equivalent and the Model Context Protocol (MCP); least-privilege tool 
permissions, human approval for every consequential action, audit trails and rollback; reusable 
agent templates for drafting, document scrutiny and request routing 
Evaluation & Safety 
• With the QA Lead, build golden datasets and specialisation-appropriate metrics, set release 
thresholds, and run subgroup analysis across languages, document types, demographics or 
acoustic conditions 
• With the AI Safety team, test services for prompt injection, presentation attacks, adversarial 
inputs and leakage of personal data before release 
Deployment & Reuse 
• Deploy services through the AI platform and gateway, publish them to the service catalogue 
with documentation and SLAs, and contribute models and evaluation sets to AIKosh 
Vendor Oversight 
• Review designs, code and evaluation evidence of vendor teams, and recommend acceptance or 
rejection of deliverables 
Responsible AI & Privacy 
• Apply anonymisation, data minimisation and DPDPA 2023 requirements, with stricter handling 
for biometric data in Computer Vision, and document models through model cards and 
evaluation records 
Technical Competencies 
 
• Common: Python (expert level), PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, PEFT and TRL 
(LoRA, QLoRA, DPO, GRPO); vLLM or SGLang; MLflow, Docker, Git; evaluation design 
with bootstrap confidence intervals; Langfuse or Arize Phoenix 
• Indic Language AI: AI4Bharat models (IndicConformer, IndicTrans2, IndicBERT, Indic 
Parler-TTS), Sarvam models and Bhashini services; code-mixed and transliterated text 
• NLP & Document AI: document-parsing models such as PaddleOCR-VL, MinerU or GLM-
OCR, and PP-OCR; Docling; vision-language models such as the Qwen-VL family; hybrid 
search and re-ranking; pgvector, Qdrant or Milvus; RAGAS or DeepEval; Microsoft Presidio 
• Speech AI: IndicConformer, Whisper, NVIDIA Parakeet or Canary; NVIDIA NeMo or 
ESPnet; Silero VAD, pyannote; WebRTC, SIP, Pipecat or LiveKit Agents; WhatsApp Business 
Platform; WER and CER tooling 
 
* Computer Vision: ४0,026 or YOLOII, RF-DETR, SAM 3, DINOv3, SigLIP 2; ArcFace or
AdaFace with InsightFace; ISO/IEC 3007-3 presentation-attack metrics; image-manipulation
detection (such as TruFor); ONNX Runtime, TensorRT, LiteRT

* Agentic AI: LangGraph, LlamaIndex, OpenAI Agents SDK or Google ADK; MCP; Temporal;
Open Policy Agent; trajectory and tool-use evaluation (Inspect, DeepEval or LangSmith);
prompt-injection testing for agents (such as AgentDojo)

* Governance: DPDPA 2023, MeitY Responsible AI advisory, IndiaAI Safe & Trusted AI
framework, OWASP Top 0 for LLM Applications


 
Designation: Data Science Lead 
 
 
Specialisation Positions Focus 
Predictive Analytics 1 Forecasting, risk and propensity scoring, and early-
warning models 
Fraud & Risk Analytics 1 Fraud and anomaly detection, entity resolution and 
network analysis on claims and transactions 
 
Role Summary 
 
The Data Science Lead will lead a data science team in one specialisation, owning the predictive, risk 
and anomaly models that government departments use for operational decisions, and providing technical 
oversight of vendor teams. The role requires statistical depth, sound judgement on the choice of method, 
rigorous validation with quantified uncertainty, and the ability to explain models to senior decision 
makers and investigators. 
 
Educational Qualification 
 
• B.Tech./B.E., M.Tech./M.S. or M.Sc. in Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Computer 
Science, Data Science or a related quantitative discipline  
• Ph.D. or published applied work in statistics, econometrics, forecasting or fraud analytics is 
highly desirable 
• Certifications are not mandatory; demonstrated work, as listed under Minimum Evidence at 
Screening, shall carry greater weight 
• Candidates with strong verifiable work (Kaggle Master level or above, published research or 
significant open-source contributions) will be considered in lieu of formal qualification 
Experience 
 
• 8+ years in data science, statistics or applied machine learning (12+ years preferred); minimum 
4 years building models in the chosen specialisation used in operational decisions 
• At least 3 years leading data science teams or projects, including review of other data scientists' 
models 
• Demonstrable ownership of at least two predictive, risk or fraud systems in production, 
with documented validation and measured outcomes 
• Predictive Analytics: experience with hierarchical, spatial or panel data, and with missing, 
delayed or inconsistent data 
• Fraud & Risk Analytics: experience detecting fraud or anomalies with few labels, including 
record linkage across sources and graph-based detection 
• Experience with causal inference or programme evaluation is a strong plus; experience in the 
public sector, health, agriculture, banking, insurance or payments is a plus 
Key Responsibilities 
 
Problem Formulation 
• Translate business questions into well-defined problems with a clear decision, baseline and 
evaluation metric 
• Assess data feasibility, including coverage, reporting delays, label quality, leakage and bias, and 
advise where the data is insufficient for the objective 
 
Specialisation Responsibilities 
• Predictive Analytics: time-series, hierarchical and spatial forecasts at district, state and 
national level, with reconciliation across levels and backtesting; risk, propensity and 
prioritisation scores; early-warning thresholds designed with the operational teams who will use 
them 
• Fraud & Risk Analytics: fraud typologies defined with investigators; rules combined with 
unsupervised, semi-supervised and positive-unlabelled learning; entity resolution across 
individuals, bank accounts, addresses and documents; graph analysis of linked cases; risk scores 
with reason codes and review queues sized to investigator capacity; checks against identity, tax, 
document and bank-account records 
Validation, Uncertainty & Monitoring 
• Validate models with leakage-free schemes, and quantify uncertainty through prediction 
intervals, calibration and conformal prediction 
• Monitor drift after go-live, including adaptation by fraudsters, and assess whether deployed 
models improved outcomes using experiments or quasi-experimental methods 
Responsible AI & Governance 
• Audit fairness across regions and population groups, provide explanations for decisions 
affecting individuals, and maintain model cards, evaluation records and audit trails 
• Apply anonymisation and data minimisation in compliance with DPDPA 2023 
Analytics Products 
• Deliver dashboards and analytical services on a shared metric layer, with the Data Engineering 
Lead and the engineering team 
Team Leadership & Vendor Oversight 
• Lead in-house data scientists, review their work, and remain hands-on 
• Provide technical oversight of vendor teams, and recommend acceptance or rejection of 
deliverables 
Technical Competencies 
 
• Statistics & Causal Inference: generalised linear, hierarchical and Bayesian models (PyMC); 
A/B testing, difference-in-differences, synthetic control, regression discontinuity (DoWhy, 
EconML) 
• Machine Learning: XGBoost, LightGBM and CatBoost; tabular foundation models (TabPFN); 
explainability (SHAP); calibration 
• Uncertainty: prediction intervals, conformal prediction (MAPIE), bootstrap methods 
• Predictive Analytics: ARIMA, ETS and state-space models; hierarchical reconciliation 
(MinT); statsforecast, Darts or GluonTS; time-series foundation models (Chronos-2, TimesFM); 
GeoPandas and H3 
• Fraud & Risk Analytics: PyOD, Isolation Forest, autoencoders; Splink, Zingg or Dedupe with 
transliteration-aware matching of Indian names and addresses; Neo4j, NetworkX, PyTorch 
Geometric or DGL; weak supervision and Cleanlab; precision at k and cost-sensitive metrics 
• Data & Engineering: advanced SQL, PySpark, Polars or DuckDB; Python with pytest, Git, 
MLflow and DVC 
• Communication: Superset, Power BI or Tableau; explaining limitations and uncertainty to non-
technical audiences 
• Governance: Fairlearn; DPDPA 2023; MeitY Responsible AI advisory

calibration/uncertainty evaluation for RAG systems and generative outputs across teams 
 Run bias and fairness audits using quantitative metrics — demographic parity, equalised 
odds, calibration, subgroup accuracy.

impact assessments on team deliverables 
 Author the technical safety evaluation content in model cards, dataset sheets, 
bias/hallucination/safety evaluation reports, and Responsible AI evidence per the MeitY 
Responsible AI advisory and the IndiaAI Safe & Trusted AI framework. 
 
AI Security Architecture & Threat Modelling 
 Own AI-specific threat modelling end-to-end for all pod systems under development — 
STRIDE, MITRE ATT&CK, MITRE ATLAS and OWASP Top 10 for LLMs — 
including data pipelines, retrieval sources, model artefacts, prompt paths, tool interfaces 
and output surfaces 
 Review deployment configurations across IndiaAI Compute, on-premise/sovereign GPU 
and CSP-API paths for AI -specific security risks; recommend controls and defensive 
patterns 
 Contribute AI security and Responsible AI requirements to NeGD RFQs, RDRs and 
procurement documents; review empanelled-agency proposals for AI security posture 
 
Cross-Programme Advisory, Upskilling & Governance Input 
 Advise each team’s AI QA Engineer on safety and Responsible AI test design, sa mple 
selection, evaluation metrics and evidence capture 
 Brief and upskill teams on AI-specific security concerns and Responsible AI controls. 
 
Research, Publication & Knowledge Transfer 
 Track adversarial ML, LLM safety, agentic -AI safety and Responsible AI  research 
literature; translate relevant findings into team -usable checks, controls and evaluation 
additions 
 Maintain the programme’s open -source AI safety testing toolkit; deposit reusable 
notebooks, evaluation harnesses and playbooks to OpenForge, and publish reusable 
evaluation sets and safety artefacts to AIKosh under standard metadata for reuse
